Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.17150 of 2019
Order:

This Writ Petition is filed with the following prayer:
" For the reasons stated in the accompanying affidavit, the petitioners pay that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to issue writ, order or direction more particularly in the nature of Writ of Mandamus aggrieved by the inaction on the part of respondents particularly respondents 7 to 11 on petitioners' representation dated 29-11-2018 submitted for payment of compensation to the petitioners for their respective lands admeasuring Ac.56.04 gts respectively covered by Survey No.39/1 of Thottipampu Village in Annapureddypally Mandal in Bhadradri Kothagudem District

pursuant to Publication of Preliminary Notification dated 16-06-2018 in Proc.No.A4/65/2018 issued by the 8th respondent and Consent Award dt.21-11-2018 in File No.B/403/2018 issued by the 7th respondent as the said lands were acquired for the purpose of excavation of Gravity Canal for Sitarama Lift Irrigation Project and consequently direct the respondents to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners for their said acquired lands and pass such other order...

" 
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for land Acquisition,
learned Government Pleader for Irrigation and Command Area Development, learned Government Pleader for Social Welfare appearing on behalf of official respondents and Sri J.R.Manohar Rao,
learned Sanding Counsel for Endowments appearing on behalf of respondent No.12, and perused the record.
CASE OF THE PETITIONERS 3.

Petitioners contend that the 12th respondent-Temple holds vast extent of agricultural landed property in Sy.Nos.39/1, 39/2 and 39/3 of Annadaivam Revenue village in Chandrugonda Mandal of Khammam District; that the petitioners and prior to them, their fore-fathers have been cultivating different extents of land since time immemorial as the said lands are situated in the notified scheduled area; that out of the said extent of land held by the respondent No.12-Temple,
respondent No.7 had acquired the land to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts in Sy.No.39/1 of Thottipampu village in Annapureddypally Mandal in Bhadradri Kothagudem District (erstwhile Khammam District) pursuant to publication of Preliminary Notification dated 16-06-2018 and thereafter passing a Consent Award dated 21-11-2018 for the purpose of excavation of Gravity Canal for Sita Sunnam Peddiraju vs State Of Telangana on 30 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119482157/
1 Rama Lift Irrigation Project (for short 'SRLI Project').

sentences.text: 4. Petitioners further contend that though the 12th respondent- Temple is the pattedar of the said land, since the subject land acquired was being cultivated by them and their fore-fathers, they are entitled to the compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act').

sentences.text:
5. Petitioners further contend that since the subject land acquired by the respondents are in their possession and cultivation, they are also entitled for Rehabilitation and Resettlement (for short 'R&R') benefits under the Act; that the fact of petitioners being tenants of respondent No.12 is admitted by respondents by the counter-affidavit filed in W.P.No.27242 of 2016 filed by them assailing the action of respondents in undertaking to conduct Enjoyment Survey; and that the said fact is also been taken note of by this Court in its order dated 24-07-2019 passed in W.P.No.29631 of 2017 filed against the action of respondent No.12 in seeking to evict the petitioners from the subject land for non-payment of rent.
6.

Petitioners further contend that since the factum of tenancy is not in dispute, mere non-payment or default in payment of rent would not by itself make the petitioners, strangers to the subject land and as such, the petitioners are covered by the term "person interested" as defined in Section 3(x) of the Act.

7. Petitioners further contend that the respondent authorities having received the rent from the petitioners, cannot now turn around to deny the claim of petitioners for receiving the compensation as tenants of the subject property.

8. It is also the further contention of the petitioners that in the Enjoyment Survey conducted by the respondent Revenue authorities, which is subject matter of W.P.No.27242 of 2016, petitioners are shown as in possession of the land belonging to the 12th respondent-Temple; and that the 12th respondent seeking to evict the petitioners from the subject land for giving the same on lease to non-tribals through public auction compelling the petitioners to approach this Court by filing a Writ Petition vide W.P.No.29631 of 2017 would only go to show that while the petitioners are tenants of respondent No.12, the said fact is being denied only in order to defeat the claim of petitioners for award of compensation/extending benefits of R&R under the Act.

9. It is also the further contention of the petitioners that though after issuing Preliminary Notification, the respondent authorities in particular respondent No.7 had invited the petitioners for negotiations for passing the Consent Award under Section 23-A of the Act, however, had excluded the petitioners from apportionment of compensation amount under the Award dated 21-11-2018;

thus, the petitioners have approached the respondent authorities and submitted representation dated 29-11-2018 and sought for conducting enquiry by issuing advance notice to petitioners enabling them to place evidence and prove their contentions for being considered as 'person interested' in order to claim compensation/benefits of R&R; and that in spite of petitioners submitting the aforesaid representation, no action thereon is taken till date and as such, petitioners are compelled to file the present Writ Petition.

11. Counter-affidavit on behalf of respondent Nos.2 and 12 are filed.

12. Learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.12 would contend that the subject land belongs to the respondent No.12-Temple and as such, the compensation awarded in respect of the land acquired by the respondent No.7 under the Award dated 21-11-2018 cannot be apportioned to the petitioners; that as per Section 82(5) of the Telangana Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987 (for short the 'Endowments Act'), the lease of land belonging to or given or endowed for the purpose of any charitable or religious Order dated 11-10-2011 in Civil Appeal NO.8539 of 2011 (Arising out of SLP(C) institutions or endowment as defined under the said Act are excluded from the purview of the provisions of the Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950 (for short 'Tenancy Act'), and thus, the petitioners cannot claim the benefit of Section 102(G) of the Tenancy Act.
13.

sentences.text: By drawing the attention to the representation submitted by the petitioners dated 29-11-2018 would contend that the petitioners by their own admission admit to the fact of the lands under their cultivation, though as encroachers in terms of section 83 of the Endowments Act, are not covered by the acquisition undertaken by the 7th respondent authority and covered by the Award dated 21-11-2018 and as such, the petitioners are not entitled for any compensation.

14. Learned Standing Counsel would further submit that the petitioners being in arrears of lease in respect lands under their cultivation even for the earlier period, on the respondent authorities initiating action for their eviction, had approached this Court by filing a Writ Petition vide W.P.No.29631 of 2017, and this Court by order dated 24-07-2019 directed the Writ petitioners to pay the entire due amount of lease for the lands for which they have been cultivating (other than the land of an extent of Ac.56.04 gts acquired by the Government for the purpose of SRLI Project); and that on knowing of the 12th respondent-Temple being awarded with compensation, are falsely claiming that the land acquired is under their cultivation.

15. Learned Standing Counsel would further contend that it is only the protected tenants, who are entitled to receive compensation in respect of the lands acquired belonging to the land owner and since petitioners are to be treated as 'encroachers' in terms of Section 83 of the Endowments Act inasmuch as petitioners are not tenants under the respondent No.12-Temple and submitted a representation claiming that their lands are not acquired, would by itself disentitle the petitioners from maintaining the present Writ Petition.
16. In support of his contention, learned Standing Counsel has placed reliance on the decision in Ch.Satyanarayana & Ors Vs. Land Acquisition Officer-cum-Sub-Collector & Others 2.

18. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition would further contend that as per Rule 9(g)
of the Rules, the lease is liable to cancelled if the terms and conditions of the lease deed or the conditions prescribed under the Rules are violated. 2008(2) ALD 679 19.

It is also contended by the learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition that since the petitioners have not placed any lease deed in writing as required under Rule 18 of the Rules, the petitioners cannot claim themselves to be the tenants of respondent No.12-temple as the said tenancy is not recognizable tenancy either in the statute or Constitution or Common law in order to claim as 'Person having interest'.
20.

Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition would further contend that since the petitioners by the representation dated 29-11-2018 submitted to respondent Nos.7 to 11 having sought for the lands under their cultivation to be acquired along with the land to an extent of Ac.56.04 cents, are precluded / prevented from claiming apportionment of compensation paid to the 12th respondent in respect of other land which is not under the cultivation of petitioners.
21.

Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition on behalf of respondent No.2 would contend that based on the proposals from the Executive Engineer, SRLI Project, Div.No.3, Sathupally for acquisition of land in Annadaivam village of Annapureddypally Mandal of Bhadradri Kothagudem District for construction of Gravity Canal under SRLI Project, the Survey Department had conducted Enjoyment Survey in Annadaivam Revenue village and submitted Enjoyment report along with Sub-Division Records to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts; that as per the Sub-Division record and as per report dated 10-08-2017, the land under acquisition is covered by Sy.No.39/1; and on the basis of the aforesaid report and records submitted by respondent No.11, proposals were sent to respondent No.8, who had approved for initiation of land acquisition proceedings and approved the Preliminary Notification on 16-06-2018 and that upon such approval, the Preliminary Notification was published in the District Gazette on 19-06-2018 and also in two news papers.
22.

On the basis of the counter-affidavit, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition would further contend that the Preliminary Notification was also displayed/published at the Gram Panchayat Office, Annadaivam, Tahsildar Office, Revenue Divisional Office and Collectorate,
Bhadradri-Kothagudem on 26-10-2018 calling for objections from the 'persons interested' within a period of 60 days from the date of notification issued under Section 11(1) of the Act.
23.

Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition would further contend that the petitioners did not submit any objection to the proposals made in the Preliminary Notification as published,
within the time prescribed under the Act and only after expiry of the statutory period of 60 days Sunnam Peddiraju vs State Of Telangana on 30 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119482157/
4 from the date of Notification, have submitted Objection Petition on 29-11-2018; and that since the objections were submitted beyond the statutory period prescribed, the contention of the petitioners that the respondents have not considered the Objection Petition, is incorrect.

sentences.text: 24. By the counter-affidavit, it is further stated that the pahanis for the years 1970 to 2012 records the name of the respondent No.12 as owner and possessor of the aforesaid extent of land and that the claim of the petitioners has not been noted in 'enjoyer' column and as such, the petitioners cannot be treated as in possession and enjoyment of the subject land validly for them to claim so as to treat them as 'person interested' in order to be eligible to claim compensation.

25. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition further contends that since the subject land is an endowed property before the same is acquired, the respondent authorities have approached this Court by filing a Writ Petition vide W.P.No.10547 of 2006 and obtained permission on 02-05-2018 with condition that compensation amount shall be deposited with the Temple and that based on the aforesaid permission granted by this Court, Notification has been issued on 03-07-2018 and after following due process of law, the Award has been passed on 21-11-2018 and total compensation amount has been deposited to the account of respondent No.12-Temple.
26.

By the counter-affidavit, it is further contended that the provisions of the A.P.Tenancy Act, 1956 have no application to the endowment properties and having regard to language of Section 3(x) of the Act, it is for the petitioners to establish that they meet the requirements of the provisions of the Amendment Act more particularly Section 81 and 82 and the Rules framed thereunder for being considered as subsisting tenancy and in the absence of petitioners establishing the said fact, are not entitled for any relief from this Court.

27. Learned Government Pleader would further contend that in the Award dated 21-11-2018, since the names of the petitioners have not been mentioned as 'enjoyers' of the 12th respondent's land,
they are not entitled for any apportionment as noted in the Award.

28. Learned Government Pleader thus submits that the petitioners, on learning of the land of 12th respondent-temple having been acquired and being in receipt of compensation amount and inasmuch as their lands are not acquired, though being encroachers, are laying claim for compensation while continuing with the illegal occupation of 12th respondent's lands and as such,
the authorities taking note of the fact that the petitioners did not give consent in Form G1 format as per G.O.Ms.No.120 Revenue (JA&LA) Department dated 30-06-2017, are not entitled to claim any compensation inasmuch as the land to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts has been consented to be acquired by respondent No.12 pursuant to permission granted by this Court.
29.
Thus, on the basis of the above submissions, learned Government Pleaders and learned Standing Counsel seek for dismissal of the Writ Petition.
30. I have taken note of respective contentions urged.

sentences.text: Though, the petitioners in the present Writ Petition have sought for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus against the inaction of respondent Nos.7 to 11 in considering the representation dated 29-11-2018 stated to have been submitted by them, it is to be noted that the petitioners by the aforesaid representation at more than one place i.e. at para 3 and 4 have categorically admitted to the fact of the lands under their occupation and cultivation have not been notified for the purpose of land acquisition.

The said claim of the petitioners by the aforesaid representation itself would show that the land to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts in Sy.No.39/1of Annadivam village covered by the Preliminary Notification and the Award does not include the land under cultivation of the petitioners in order to be considered as 'person interested' so as to be entitled for receiving any compensation.

32. Further, from a perusal of the Award dated 21-11-2018 as passed by the 7th respondent authority, it is to be noted that prior to issuing Preliminary Notification, a survey was stated to have been undertaken wherein it was found that the land to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts is shown as 'patta land' falling in Sy.No.39/1 with its sub-division numbers; that at present 27 farmers (wrongly mentioned as pattedars instead of farmers) are partially loosing their lands to an extent of 56.04 gts;
and that the said farmers have agreed to give their lands on payment of reasonable price as per the Act.

The award further indicates that all the 27 farmers, whose lands were partially been affected by the acquisition to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts having agreed to give their lands by expressing their willingness to settle the claim through negotiations, the 7th respondent had passed the Consent Award under Section 23A of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Re- settlement (Telangana Amendment) Act, 2016.
33.

Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Re- settlement (Telangana Amendment) Act, 2016
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Though, petitioners claim that 27 pattadars as mentioned in the Award under the head 'Arrival of Compensation Payment' includes the names of the petitioners, no material is placed before this Court to show either the petitioners having given their consent in Form-G1 format as enjoyers as prescribed under G.O.Ms.No.120 dated 30-06-2017 nor names of such 27 alleged pattadars, whose lands are stated to be partially affected by the land acquisition to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts being affected in order to be eligible to receive the lumpsum payment of compensation.

34. It is also to be noted that the effect of Section 82 of the Endowments Act and its amendment was subject matter of consideration before the Apex Court in State of A.P. and others Vs. Nallamilli Rami Reddi and others 3 and the Apex Court summed up holding as under:
"15.

entities.text: State of A.P. and others Vs. Nallamilli Rami Reddi and others 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
We may sum up the upshot of our discussion:
1. That charitable or religious institutions or endowments fall into a separate category and form a class by themselves.
If that is so, tenants coming under them also form a separate class.
Therefore, they can be treated differently from others.

In operation of the Act it is possible that it may result in hardship to some of the tenants but that by itself will not be a consideration to condemn the Act.
Sunnam Peddiraju vs State Of Telangana on 30 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119482157/
6

entities.text: Sunnam Peddiraju vs State Of Telangana on 30 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The manner in which the charitable or religious institution or endowment would deal with the properties that are resumed after the provisions of Section 82 of the Act come into force by cancelling the existing leases, is in the region of speculation.

4. Fresh tenancy can be entered into and there is no material before the court as to what was the rent paid by tenants at the time when the Act came into force, in terms of Section 18(2) of the Act or as provided under the Andhra Act or under the Telangana Act.

In the absence of such a material, it would be hazardous for the court to reach any conclusion, one way or the other, to state that the tenants would be frozen and, therefore, there is no likelihood of charitable or religious institution or endowment getting higher rents.
If there is no material one way or the other, the presumption that the Act is good should prevail.

5. It is a matter of policy with the legislature as to whether all provisions of the Tenancy Acts should be exempt in its application to the charitable or religious institution or endowment in their entirety.
6. The identification of "landless poor persons" and protection given to them is justified as enunciated earlier.
7. It will be very difficult to predict at this stage that the result of Section 82 of the Act would be so hazardous as not to achieve the object for which it was enacted.
It would not only result in displacing the old tenants by new tenants, it may also achieve other social objectives in another manner.

If appropriate provisions are made under the Rules and if the leases are given to small holders of land,
another social objective could be achieved.
8. In what manner charitable or religious institution or endowment would deal with matters of this nature is mere guesswork at this stage.
On some hypothetical approach the High Court could not have declared a law to be invalid."

35. The Apex Court while observing as above, had set aside the order of the erstwhile High Court for the composite State of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh dated 03-10-1989 in W.A.No.1267 of 1989 and batch passed in S.Narayana Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh and others 4.
36.

entities.text: S.Narayana Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the Apex Court also negatived the additional contentions raised and held that the object of the Act is to resume lands in the hands of existing tenants for better management.

37. It is thereafter Section 82(5) of the Endowments Act has been added by Act No.27 of 2002 w.e.f.
26-08-2002.
38.

Subsequent to the aforesaid decision of the Apex Court, the erstwhile High Court for the Composite State of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh Court in Ch.Satayanarayana (2 supra) had held that Section 82 of the Endowments Act rendered all the endowments of the temple lands given by the charitable and religious institutions invalid from the date of coming into force of Section 82(1) of the Endowments Act and lease in respect of temple lands stands cancelled as Tenancy Act has no application, and thus, the tenant is not entitled to a share in the compensation.

39 . Further, a Division Bench erstwhile High Court for the Composite State of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh in The Executive Officer, Sri Kanaka Mahalakshmi Ammavaru Devasthanam Vs.
Bokka Venkata Rao & Others 5 had held that in view of law as enunciated by the Nallamilli Rami Reddi (supra), a tenant under Endowments Act is not entitled for any right or benefit under the Act and it cannot be said that he is a tenant in respect of Temple land under the Act as his tenancy stood cancelled w.e.f. 28-05-1987 by operation of law and therefore is not entitled to claim to compensation as cultivating tenant.

sentences.text: 40. Though, the petitioners claim to be tenants of the lands belonging to the 12th respondent-Temple, it is to be noted that by virtue of the judgment of the Supreme Court and subsequent addition of Section 82(5) of the Endowments Act, the endowed lands are excluded from the operation / applicability of the provisions of the Tenancy Act, and the petitioners cannot be treated as tenants, be it as protected or otherwise.

In view of the 2010 SCC online AP 608 above, the reliance by the petitioners on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajendra Vassudev Deshprabhu (1 supra) is of little assistance to advance their case.

41. Having regard to the position of law as detailed above, the claim of the petitioners to be treated as tenants of lands belonging to the respondent No.12-Temple cannot be accepted, and are thus not entitled to claim any compensation from and out of the compensation paid to the 12th respondent-Temple in respect of land admeasuring Ac.56.04 gts acquired.

42. However, taking note of the fact that the Award as passed by the 7th respondent recognizes 27 farmers (wrongly mentioned as pattedars) partially loosing their lands and having agreed to give their lands on payment of reasonable price, this Court is of the view that respondent authorities are to be directed to verify whether the names of the petitioners are forming part of said 27 farmers (stated to be wrongly mentioned as pattadars in the Award), as the Award does not disclose the names of the said 27 farmers, which is stated to be forming part of Award Enquiry, as the same is not placed before this Court.

43. Thus, this Court is of the view that if the list of the awardees as confirmed by the Award Enquiry includes the names of the petitioners as 'enjoyers' of the subject land, then only the petitioners can be considered as 'person interested' as defined under Section 3(x) of the Act for being entitled to receive the R&R benefits under the Act as amended by Telangana Amendment Act 21 of 2017.
44. Subject to above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
45. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending if any shall stand closed.
_ _ _ T. VINOD KUMAR, J Date: 30.10 .2024

the authorities taking note of the fact that the petitioners did not give consent in Form G1 format as per G.O.Ms.No.120 Revenue (JA&LA) Department dated 30-06-2017, are not entitled to claim any compensation inasmuch as the land to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts has been consented to be acquired by respondent No.12 pursuant to permission granted by this Court.
29.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The said claim of the petitioners by the aforesaid representation itself would show that the land to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts in Sy.No.39/1of Annadivam village covered by the Preliminary Notification and the Award does not include the land under cultivation of the petitioners in order to be considered as 'person interested' so as to be entitled for receiving any compensation.
Though, petitioners claim that 27 pattadars as mentioned in the Award under the head 'Arrival of Compensation Payment' includes the names of the petitioners, no material is placed before this Court to show either the petitioners having given their consent in Form-G1 format as enjoyers as prescribed under G.O.Ms.No.120 dated 30-06-2017 nor names of such 27 alleged pattadars, whose lands are stated to be partially affected by the land acquisition to an extent of Ac.56.04 gts being affected in order to be eligible to receive the lumpsum payment of compensation.
Further, the Apex Court also negatived the additional contentions raised and held that the object of the Act is to resume lands in the hands of existing tenants for better management.
Subsequent to the aforesaid decision of the Apex Court, the erstwhile High Court for the Composite State of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh Court in Ch.Satayanarayana (2 supra) had held that Section 82 of the Endowments Act rendered all the endowments of the temple lands given by the charitable and religious institutions invalid from the date of coming into force of Section 82(1) of the Endowments Act and lease in respect of temple lands stands cancelled as Tenancy Act has no application, and thus, the tenant is not entitled to a share in the compensation.
(1990) 1 ALT 237 Sunnam Peddiraju vs State Of Telangana on 30 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119482157/
40. Though, the petitioners claim to be tenants of the lands belonging to the 12th respondent-Temple, it is to be noted that by virtue of the judgment of the Supreme Court and subsequent addition of Section 82(5) of the Endowments Act, the endowed lands are excluded from the operation / applicability of the provisions of the Tenancy Act, and the petitioners cannot be treated as tenants, be it as protected or otherwise.
41. Having regard to the position of law as detailed above, the claim of the petitioners to be treated as tenants of lands belonging to the respondent No.12-Temple cannot be accepted, and are thus not entitled to claim any compensation from and out of the compensation paid to the 12th respondent-Temple in respect of land admeasuring Ac.56.04 gts acquired.
43. Thus, this Court is of the view that if the list of the awardees as confirmed by the Award Enquiry includes the names of the petitioners as 'enjoyers' of the subject land, then only the petitioners can be considered as 'person interested' as defined under Section 3(x) of the Act for being entitled to receive the R&R benefits under the Act as amended by Telangana Amendment Act 21 of 2017.
